travel.name: Travel
travel.text: The party travels. Roll 1d6 to see if they get lost. If they are lost, a Wilderness Action is needed to recover. Otherwise they reach the next point.

explore.name: Explore
explore.text: One or more members search a large area for hidden features or scout ahead. This may discover a location or feature. Leaving the area still needs Travel.

supply.name: Supply
supply.text: The party hunts, fishes, or forages for 1d4 Rations, each lasting 3 uses. Each added participant brings a bigger bounty.

make_camp.name: Make Camp
make_camp.text: The party sets up camp. Each member and mount consumes a Ration. A lookout rotation is set. Members who rest remove all Fatigue.

resupply.name: Resupply
resupply.text: The party spends gold and a full watch at a home or small village to buy basic supplies.

name: Wilderness Events
rows: Roll on an encounter table for that terrain or location, then roll NPC reactions if applicable.
A clue, spoor, or indication of a nearby encounter, locality, or hidden feature, or information about a nearby area.
A shift in weather or terrain.
The party faces a choice that costs a resource (rations or tools), time, or effort.
A barrier forces effort, care, or delays. This costs extra time (and an additional Wilderness Action) or Fatigue.
The party finds food, treasure, or useful resources. The Warden may instead reveal the area's primary feature.

name: Spring Weather
rows: Add a Fatigue or add one watch to the journey (gusting winds, rain showers, sweltering heat, chill air).
Add a Fatigue or add +1 watch, and increase terrain Difficulty by a step (thunderstorms, lightning, rain, muddy ground).
Add a Fatigue and +1 watch, and increase terrain Difficulty by a step (blizzards, freezing winds, flooding, mud slides).
